note: ADR-017 §5's member sets, as one artifact, transcribed from the ADR.
Read by BOTH sides and generated by NEITHER: the TypeScript reader's test checks its own
MANIFEST_KEY_SETS constant against this file, and the Rust writer's test checks an emitted
manifest against it. The same discipline style-agreement.json uses for style resolution.
Why it exists: a writer and a reader that each pass their own hand-maintained table can still
disagree with each other. Editing the reader and its own test keeps the JS suite green while
every real bundle becomes unreadable; editing the writer and its own table keeps the Rust suite
green while the reader still refuses. Two tables guarantee only that neither side can move
without its own test failing, which is not the same as the two agreeing. This file is where
they agree.
SCOPE: key sets only. This artifact says which members an object has, never what type each
one holds, so two sets being identical here does NOT mean the members are identically typed,
and this file cannot catch a type drifting between the reader and the writer.
The live case, ADR-017 Corrigendum 1 (2026-08-06): license_declared_by_source.license is
string-or-null -- a source may declare attribution and/or redistribution and name no license,
and null is that absence -- while license_declared_by_operator.license is a non-empty string,
because an operator states a license or makes no declaration at all. Neither set changed.
Per-member types are the ADR's, and each side enforces them in its own code, at these sites:
writer  kernel/src/publish/mod.rs::admit_license (refuses a blank operator license) and
kernel/src/bundle/mod.rs (DeclaredByOperator holds a String, so a null is not
representable), asserted by kernel/tests/publish.rs and the modules' unit tests;
reader  renderer/bundle-viewer/src/manifest.ts::licenseBlock via nonEmptyStr, asserted by
scripts/manifest.test.mjs.
That is two enforcements of one rule written down in the ADR, not one shared artifact -- a
weaker guarantee than the key sets have, and named here rather than left to be assumed.
A THIRD CLASS this artifact cannot express, added with ADR-017 Corrigendum 3 (2026-08-07):
REFERENTIAL INTEGRITY. viewer_license.notice_path must equal the `path` of one entry in
viewer[] -- a relation between two members, not a key set and not a type. Both sides enforce
it in their own code and each has its own negative test, at these sites:
writer  kernel/src/publish/mod.rs::admit_viewer_license, against the supplied ViewerAssets.
This is the refusal that fires, and kernel/tests/publish.rs asserts it. A second,
unreachable backstop in `run` re-checks against the EMITTED viewer[] list: both
sites share one `viewer_bundle_path`, and the emission maps 1:1 over the same
assets, so the early check passing implies the later one passing. NO TEST covers
that branch -- reaching it needs a code change that breaks the 1:1 mapping -- and
saying so is better than implying coverage that does not exist;
reader  renderer/bundle-viewer/src/manifest.ts::viewerLicenseBlock, asserted by
scripts/manifest.test.mjs.
The mutation sweep in manifest.test.mjs walks key sets, so it would NOT catch a notice_path
naming no viewer asset. That is why the dedicated negative tests exist.
